 After Campaigning for Democrats, Barack Obama Spent an Evening with His Daughters as the Party Prepared to Control Both Chambers of Congress
 By 
 Nadia Santiago 
 Updated 3 days ago, 
 November 9, 2026 
 Barack Obama joined Malia, 28, and Sasha, 25, for dinner on November 6, 3 days after the election that returned both the House and Senate to Democratic control. The former president, 65, arrived with his daughters and a Secret Service detail. There’s no confirmation that the dinner was arranged to celebrate the results.
 Obama had spent the closing weeks of the campaign urging voters to check President Donald Trump’s administration. On October 24, he rallied in Cleveland and Detroit, supporting candidates including Sherrod Brown, Amy Acton, Jocelyn Benson and Abdul El-Sayed. On October 28, he campaigned in Morrow, Georgia, for Sen. Jon Ossoff and gubernatorial nominee Keisha Lance Bottoms.
 After the election, Obama praised candidates who’d competed across an expanded map. “These results were only possible because outstanding candidates stepped forward in every region of the country — including in areas once considered long shots,” he wrote. Acton, El-Sayed and Bottoms were among the candidates he backed who won their races.
 The family dinner also followed a campaign moment when Obama brought up raising his daughters while defending his joke about Trump’s White House decor. At the Georgia rally, he said: “I am the father of two daughters; do you think I could have survived their childhood without the Cheesecake Factory?”
 In a June 24 interview, Obama described trying to keep pace with his now-adult daughters: “I can barely keep up with them at the dinner table now, if I was their contemporary, I would just sit there.”
